mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate consistently signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals persistent labor market weakness that reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending slowdown in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) consistently indicates strengthening consumer confidence and residential investment, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through a positive demand shock.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening that suppresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
